newsitem.title: JAPAN: Currency market moves nervous--BOJ's Matsushita.
newsitem.headline: Currency market moves nervous--BOJ's Matsushita.

text.p: Recent movements in the foreign exchange market are rather nervous, Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.

"The currency markets are showing rather nervous movements. At the moment, however, I do not believe they (foreign exchange movements) are having a notably large impact on corporate sentiment," Matsushita said.
He added that the April current account surplus rose on the back of weakness in the yen and strong economies overseas.
"There is a strong possibility that the current account surplus will rise for a while," he said.
Meanwhile, he said, looking to the intermediate term, there are recent factors such as the strengthening of the yen and Japan's economic recovery which will work to suppress the surplus.
"It is hard to predict whether the rise in the surplus will continue," he said.
Matsushita said that it was important to think about external balances in light of achieving continued growth without inflation, which is a common goal for all countries.
The rise in Japan's net exports was one factor that triggered a favourable economic cycle in the private sector, he said.
There is a strong possibility that Japan's economic recovery will continue, he added.
"We will make efforts to manage the economy appropriately so that it will move on to a self-sustainable recovery," he said.
He said that moves in currency markets were not only determined by the current account data, but also by inflation and interest rate differentials between countries.
